about: Springbrook Hollow Farm Distillery grew out of a friendship. Dave Bannon and Mike Forcier, both bourbon enthusiasts, decided to make their own spirits on Bannon’s 200-acre former horse farm in the Adirondack foothills near Lake George, and brought in school friends Matt Colucci, Tony DeSantis and Ken Rohne. Their first bottles reached the public in 2014, beginning with vodka and gin while the whiskeys took their time in barrel.

The Adirondack Straight Rye carries a straight-whiskey designation, and the distillery states that it is aged no less than four years. Springbrook’s whiskey program works with New York-grown grain, barrels from Adirondack Barrel Cooperage in Utica and the farm’s own spring water, and the rye is bottled at 43% alcohol, or 86 proof. The producer does not publish the mash bill or say whether this rye was distilled on the farm or sourced and bottled there.

Springbrook’s own descriptions lean two ways. The product page speaks of rich, creamy caramel and toffee carried by a gentle, warming rye spice; the distillery’s spirits list calls it bold and spicy, with the peppery edge typical of rye. Taken together, they describe a rye that balances caramel sweetness against spice, bottled at a gentle strength that keeps it approachable.
facts: Adirondack spring water from the farm’s own well
